summary: Local MCP server that maps your code, docs and infrastructure into a persistent graph so coding agents understand your repository.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: codebase-memory-mcp is a local MCP server that builds a persistent knowledge graph of your repository: code, documentation, configuration and infrastructure. Coding agents query it to find the right code, follow call paths and see what a change affects.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents waste tokens and time grepping through files and still miss how pieces connect. This tool indexes the structure once and gives agents compact, targeted answers about symbols, callers, dependencies and related tests.
whoFor: Developers using Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode
Teams with large or multi-language codebases
Engineers tracing infrastructure like Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform
Anyone wanting to explore code visually
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for fast local code intelligence with 17 MCP tools, a native C backend and an optional visual explorer (CBM Lens), with all analysis staying on your machine.

overview: The install script downloads the release binary, sets up MCP configuration for detected coding agents, and adds instructions, skills, agent profiles and context hooks. Restart your agent and say "Index this project".

Queries combine symbol, text and semantic search with callers, dependencies and file outlines. It indexes documentation sections and PDFs, follows relationships through Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Ansible and more, and can compare snapshots and find related tests.

CBM Lens, in open beta, is a visual explorer started with codebase-memory-mcp daemon start --open --port=9749. Processing is local. Hooks are on by default and can be removed with install --no-hooks. The project is MIT licensed.
